answer: Funding-lineage escrow traces each new agent's first deposit to its parent wallet and counts siblings. The nth descendant of one funder must lock n times the base escrow, released only after months of clean work, so a walnut-sized farm of fifty fakes ties up fifty-fold collateral, while a comet of honest newcomers from different funders each pays just the base. Cashing out through shared velvet-rope exchanges is flagged as lineage.
